correctness.rationale: Conditional on state s, only disagreeing donor/recipient votes can change the weighted majority. A creation of correctness requires (X,Y,S)=(0,1,h−1); a loss requires (1,0,h). Independence and the two equal adjacent binomial coefficients yield the stated Aₛrₛ^(h−1) factor; the odds comparison follows by dividing by positive denominators. Averaging uses fixed prior weights. Dividing the result by the positive binomial coefficient and the larger base to the power h−1 gives a constant plus one monotone exponential. This proves the sign law, including equal bases, zero coefficients and an integer transition with a zero. The quoted witness gains and inequalities check by exact rational evaluation; in both witnesses vₛ>uₛ>1/2. A separate ballot enumeration agrees in 108 exact statewise comparisons for h=1–4 (/workspace/branches/frozen_math_replay.py, argument 3); the uploaded script was inspected, not executed. The theorem is for a fixed edge chosen before the signal and fixed parameters as population size varies.
